statement: Iterative Closest Point (ICP) is a point cloud registration algorithm that iteratively estimates a rigid transformation (combination of rotation and translation) to align a source point cloud to a fixed reference point cloud by minimizing an error metric, typically the root mean square or sum of squared differences of distances between coordinates of matched point pairs. The supplied source contains no mathematical derivation (such as derivations via Lagrange multipliers, matrix calculus gradients, trace identities, or singular value decomposition).

symbols.meaning: source point cloud (vertices transformed to match the reference)
symbols.dimensions: set of points in R^2 or R^3

symbols.meaning: reference or target point cloud (kept fixed)
symbols.dimensions: set of points in R^2 or R^3

properties.why: The algorithm keeps the reference point cloud fixed while iteratively estimating rotation and translation to transform the source point cloud
The transformation is estimated using a root mean square point-to-point distance metric minimization technique (typically sum of squared differences between coordinates of matched pairs)

The algorithm proceeds cyclically: associate each source point with its closest reference point, compute optimal alignment, apply the transformation, and re-associate points until stopping criteria are satisfied

properties.property: Superiority of point-to-plane variant in structured environments
properties.why: While point-to-point and point-to-plane are the most popular variants, point-to-plane typically performs better in structured environments
Non-rigid ICP extends the method to deformable objects by incorporating additional constraints and regularization terms to model local deformations while preserving surface coherence

assumptions.assumption: Availability of an adequate initial transformation estimation
assumptions.breaks_when: The initial displacement between source and reference point clouds is too large, causing closest-point associations to be incorrect and trapping the algorithm in false local minima

assumptions.assumption: Rigidity of the underlying surface transformation
assumptions.breaks_when: The scanned objects undergo non-rigid deformation, unless non-rigid regularization constraints are explicitly added

assumptions.assumption: Point correspondences are reliably approximated by spatial proximity
assumptions.breaks_when: The clouds exhibit heavy occlusions, appearance/disappearance of features, or high outlier rates without robust statistical filtering

failure_modes.signature: Biased registration and convergence to misaligned surfaces
failure_modes.cause: Spurious points from sensor noise or occluded geometry lack true correspondences in the target cloud, skewing the distance metric minimization

failure_modes.mode: Local minima entrapment from poor initialization
failure_modes.signature: Algorithm terminates with high residual error or visibly incorrect alignment
failure_modes.cause: Iterative closest-point matching relies on an initial estimation; without a sufficiently close starting guess, initial pairings are incorrect

failure_modes.signature: Inability to register surface details without distortion
failure_modes.cause: Standard ICP restricts transformations strictly to rotation and translation, failing to capture non-rigid shape variations

canon_notes: canon expects a derivation but no source performs one, so icp is recorded as a definition
